background_notes.fact: For sequences u,v in ell2, sum |u_k v_k| <= ||u||_ell2 ||v||_ell2. For q>1, sum over nonzero integers of |k|^(-q) is finite. Consequently H1 Fourier coefficients are absolutely summable, and the associated uniformly convergent Fourier series satisfies ||u||_infinity <= (sum <k>^(-2))^(1/2)||u||_H1. The same argument with |k|^(-1) applies to Dinv f for mean-zero f in L2.

background_notes.justification: Finite Cauchy-Schwarz followed by increasing truncations proves the sequence inequality. Integral comparison proves convergence of the positive p-series for q>1. Applying the sequence inequality to <k> hat u(k) and <k>^(-1), or hat f(k) and |k|^(-1), bounds the absolute Fourier sum. Its tails give uniform convergence and the stated supremum bound.

background_notes.fact: With the normalized Fourier Sobolev norms, ||u||_H1^2=||u||_2^2+||partial_x u||_2^2. For H1 functions u,v their product is in H1 and its weak derivative is u'v+uv'. Bounds for this product proved on polynomials extend to all H1 factors.

background_notes.justification: The norm identity is the Fourier identity 1+k^2=<k>^2, first on polynomials and then by completion. For polynomials the ordinary product rule and the L-infinity times L2 product inequality bound the derivative and the L2 norm. Approximating both factors in H1 makes their products Cauchy in H1 by the bilinear difference identity. Their limits agree with the pointwise product since the factors converge in L-infinity and L2; the derivative formula passes to the L2 limit.

background_notes.fact: For every real Sobolev order s, the multipliers S_t form a strongly continuous unitary group on H^s, preserve the zero coefficient, and preserve the reality relation between opposite Fourier coefficients.

grounds.reason: H^s uses a weighted ell2 norm.

background_notes.justification: Each multiplier has modulus one and inverse exp(-i t k^3), so it is an onto isometry. For a fixed u, the summands in ||(S_t-S_t0)u||_Hs^2 tend to zero and are bounded by 4<k>^(2s)|hat u(k)|^2, a summable sequence. A finite head and uniformly small tail prove convergence. The multiplier is one at k=0 and its value at -k is the conjugate of its value at k.

Its Fourier coefficient is the absolutely convergent convolution sum. The series sum k^2<k>^(-2pstar) and sum_(k!=0) k^(-2) are finite for pstar=23/14.

background_notes.fact: For continuous piecewise time-smooth paths with values in smooth periodic functions on a compact time interval, the Fourier series used in S003 can be differentiated termwise on each smooth piece, and the resulting identity can be integrated in any fixed Sobolev space. The fundamental theorem of calculus applies piecewise; continuity cancels shared endpoint terms.

background_notes.justification: Smooth periodic functions and the derivatives in question have Fourier coefficients decreasing faster than any fixed power, uniformly on each compact smooth time piece. Choosing a sufficiently high power makes the convolution series and its displayed derivatives uniformly absolutely convergent in a fixed Sobolev norm. Termwise differentiation is therefore legitimate. The ordinary complete-space fundamental theorem of calculus follows by integrating the continuous derivative on each piece; the endpoint values agree across adjacent pieces by continuity. Zero input modes vanish by mean-zero, so the displayed inverse-frequency factors are taken only at nonzero r,s.
